4. A separate positive operation: sampling a complete coarse record

The arbitrary-readout boundary can nevertheless be handled constructively to a useful extent.

For each supplied local POVM effect, write

$$p_i(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(M_i(x)\rho_i),
\qquad
t_i(x)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}M_i(x).$$

Choose fixed rational $0<\lambda,\theta<1$, and call $x$ rare when

$$p_i(x)<\lambda t_i(x).$$

Let

$$A_i=\sum_{x\ {\rm rare}}M_i(x),
\qquad G_i=I-A_i.$$

Define one auxiliary POVM:

$$\boxed{
Q_{i,*}=F_i=A_i+\theta G_i
=\theta I+(1-\theta)A_i,
\qquad
Q_{i,x}=(1-\theta)M_i(x)
\quad(x\ {\rm good}).
}
\tag{18}$$

This is exactly the original classical output with rare labels replaced by holes and good labels independently replaced by holes with probability $\theta$.

Every effect in (18) satisfies the initial overlap promise with

$$\lambda_*=\min(\lambda,\theta).$$

In particular, $F_i\ge\theta I$. Therefore the accepted balanced sampler generates the entire coarse record, including every revealed good label and every hole location, in its explicit short-time window. There is no separate rare-location oracle or rejection factor exponential in the number of holes.

This is an auxiliary classical construction; it adds no physical observation or preparation access.

A sparse-component guarantee

If $R$ is the original rare-site set and $Z$ the hole set, the accepted estimate

$$\Pr(S\subseteq R)\le q_r^{|S|}$$

implies

$$\boxed{
\Pr(S\subseteq Z)
\le[\theta+(1-\theta)q_r]^{|S|}.
}
\tag{19}$$

For a fixed grouping graph of degree $\Delta$, take

$$b=4(\Delta+1)^2,\qquad
\lambda=\theta=\frac1{128b}.$$

The explicit time restrictions in the report ensure

$$q_r\le6\lambda,\qquad
b[\theta+(1-\theta)q_r]<\tfrac12.$$

A connected-animal union bound then gives

$$\Pr(\text{some hole component has size}\ge L_h)
\le n\,b^{L_h-1}
[\theta+(1-\theta)q_r]^{L_h}.
\tag{20}$$

Thus $L_h=\lceil\log_2(4n/\epsilon)\rceil$ suffices for an $\epsilon/4$ tail.

The total number of holes can still be $\Theta(n)$. Equation (20) controls component sizes under the unconditional coarse law.
